narrative:
On October 29, 2026, the Karnataka High Court listed 2,990 cases across 49 judges, hearing 1,126 matters to record an overall hearing rate of 37.7%. This marks a modest improvement over the 35.4% conversion rate recorded on October 28 (1,051 heard of 2,968 scheduled), though court-wide clearance remains well below the 48.7% rate achieved on October 27. 

Judicial output varied sharply across benches. S. Rachaiah led all courts in volume by hearing 81 of 138 scheduled matters (58.7%), followed closely by G. Basavaraja with 70 hearings out of 98 listed (71.4%) and S. Vishwajith Shetty in Hall 20, who heard 71 of 95 matters (74.7%). The division bench of D. K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan also posted efficient conversion, resolving 32 of 41 cases (78.0%). In contrast, several heavy dockets stalled completely; R. Nataraj heard 0 of 119 scheduled cases, H.P. Sandesh heard 0 of 58, and C.M. Poonacha’s second list in Hall 31 saw just 5 of 127 matters taken up (3.9%).

Procedural stages drove daily activity while substantive disposals lagged. Orders represented the largest single procedural category and converted 49.2% of its docket (435 of 884 heard), a notable rebound from 33.6% the previous day. Conversely, Final Hearings experienced persistent bottlenecks, dropping to a 22.2% hearing rate (165 of 743) compared to 24.9% on October 28 and 31.9% on October 27. Admissions also contracted to 36.4% from 43.9% yesterday. Among case types, Writ Petitions dominated volume with 1,090 listings and held steady at a 34.3% hearing rate. Miscellaneous First Appeals improved markedly to 45.7% (217 of 475) from 31.5% on October 28, while Criminal Appeals saw strong traction at 58.8%. Regular Second Appeals exhibited the lowest clearance, resolving only 11 of 101 cases (10.9%).
